nested_lists.name: aus_required_conditions

fields.name: condition_category
fields.why: AU-2 — credit / income / asset / property grouping

fields.name: condition_text
fields.why: AU-2 — 'reconcile each against collected documents'. CAPTURE VERBATIM: a paraphrase breaks the match
fields.pii_note: condition text sometimes quotes borrower names or partial SSNs — do not quote identifiers

fields.name: is_prior_to_close
fields.why: AU-2 — prior-to-close vs prior-to-doc changes urgency

rejected.name: messages (a second nested list)
rejected.reason: deferred — DU's coded observation messages explain the recommendation, but AU-3's need is met by ineligibility_reasons. ~5 plumbing sites for explanatory detail

rejected.name: is_approvable / will_close
rejected.reason: a judgment, not a fact — AU-3's job

rejected.name: underwriter_notes
rejected.reason: not part of the AUS output

rejected.name: the full 1003 data echoed in the findings
rejected.reason: USE THE 1003 ITSELF. Only the AUS's STATED inputs matter, and those are the named aus_* fields — which is precisely what AU-1 compares

encoding_variations: DU vs LPA — the dominant variation. Different recommendation vocabularies (Approve/Eligible vs Accept), different message coding, different layouts
Resubmissions produce multiple findings in one file
Conditions may be numbered, bulleted, or grouped by category
Reserve requirements may be stated as months, as a dollar amount, or embedded in a condition

open_questions.q: Multiple submissions in one file (2-5 DU runs are common)
options: one extraction with a submissions list
open_questions.recommendation: separate documents — each is a distinct PDF, and a list would triple the nesting cost

open_questions.q: AU-2's condition matching is a fuzzy cross-document match
open_questions.recommendation: likely an AI tag — the schema's job is faithful capture; the matching is a SEPARATE design problem

open_questions.q: aus_* fields duplicate other documents BY DESIGN (AU-1 compares them)
open_questions.recommendation: keep the aus_ prefix — a rule must never mistake aus_qualifying_income for documented income

notes: NO v2 catalog entry — the rule floor IS the entire schema.

Only 3 rules, but AUS findings DRIVE REQUIREMENTS ACROSS THE WHOLE FILE — the required document list, reserve months, and income documentation level. AS-10 already reads it ('the required month count from DU findings'), so a fourth rule depends on it indirectly.
